cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I texted that I'd lost my job. You replied, 'What's for dinner?'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Making your dinner? Can you see why I felt like the cook?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believe you. Before you book, can you see why I heard a chore? I needed you to ask how I was.

mechanism: A grants B benign intent but withholds moving to dinner plans until B acknowledges why the wording sounded like a chore after job loss.
confusable: D75 seeks cost acknowledgment; D99 specifically distinguishes intended help from why the action was heard as hurtful.
comparison: Ambiguous dinner text after job loss differs from an expected concert attendee.
seedUse: Use D99-b correction of intended dining-out meaning; preserve A willingness to believe intent while requiring impact understood.
